### R04 entry and validation refinement

R03 is terminal. The existing rollback fixture already poisons on rollback or
connection-close uncertainty; it remains the sole transaction abstraction. Its
nested `BeginTx` uses savepoints and cannot reproduce independent snapshots,
commit visibility or non-default isolation semantics. Those are exclusion criteria.

R04.foundation.order adds a declared deterministic Go shuffle seed to `test-slice`.
Current row-list sorting means reversing ROWS does not change Go test order, and
the runner intentionally clears inherited GOFLAGS. A declared input is therefore
required for honest reordered validation. It must bind retained inputs, command
semantics and cache identity, reject invalid/non-Go selections, and preserve exact
selected symbols. No environment bypass, second runner or new acceptance gate is
introduced. Command contract v4 cuts over to v5 with all generated projections.

### R08 implementation and validation — DONE

R05 settlement was recorded before this slice began. R08 implements the adopted
REQ-805/AC-087 replacement, with further owner clarification from real pinned-runner
characterization: a module-end callback **and even the public execution promise**
precede environment teardown in Vitest 4.1.4. Successful file settlement therefore
requires the public fork-worker teardown acknowledgement and physical stop. The
small public PoolWorker adapter delegates execution and IPC to Vitest's exported
ForksPoolWorker; it accesses no private runner state. That exported class is marked
experimental upstream, so the pinned upgrade boundary includes the real teardown,
interruption and worker-accounting cases rather than assuming promise semantics.

Implementation and interface disposition:

- Compatible exact files use one fresh coordinator, one isolated fork at a time,
  normal per-file setup/teardown, and per-file public TestSpecification regexes.
  No global union of names, new registry, scheduler, resident daemon or scenario
  merging was introduced. Required project/environment/setup, owner, dependency,
  resource, fixture, timeout, failure and exclusive partitions remain separate.
- Deterministic descending-cost first-fit packing counts invocation startup and
  cleanup once and retains the existing work-unit envelope. Oversized indivisible
  files remain explicit; deadlines and resource ceilings were not increased.
  Coordinator claims add CPU=1, memory=384 MiB and process=3 to the existing worker
  profile. R06 owns final calibration, not an assertion that reservations are
  measured consumption.
- Exact project/file/full-title selection and execution policy determine
  `vitest_cohort:<digest>` identity. Existing published graph row bindings supply
  large selections; manifest, graph and unit digests are checked before reading
  catalog rows. The public ROWS limit stays 4,096 characters and is rejected
  consistently before planning/execution. Cache closures consume those same
  bindings and fail closed on conflicting legacy Go selection inputs.
- Native per-file JSON remains unchanged inside one invocation envelope. Immutable
  native checkpoints precede an atomically replaced diagnostic pointer; settled
  canonical rows use the existing publication/finalization path. File suite and
  environment teardown failures stay file-scoped. Invocation-global teardown and
  unhandled errors remain invocation failures. Cancellation/owner loss retains
  independently settled files and marks unfinished work explicitly; uncertain
  worker termination cannot start another file. The native finalizer regression
  preserves a passed Vitest row while synthesizing its cancelled sibling.
- The pinned fork runner pipes worker EOF into its supplied stderr destination.
  An invocation-owned Writable now survives worker EOF and closes after coordinator
  teardown, retaining otherwise swallowed global teardown failures. Console logs
  still reach retained stdout/stderr. Diagnostic reads use bounded anchored file
  reads and strict JSON, rejecting links, duplicate keys and replacement races.

### R01 characterization refinement

A second pass through guarded runtime branches found that a transitive DOM
reference alone does not prove a DOM requirement. `httpTransport.readCookie` and
`extensionAvailability` explicitly handle absent documents. Shared fetch fixtures
also imported DOM polling only for mock-call observation; Timeline/Query fixtures
mixed pure data builders with rendering helpers. R01.foundation now separates
those responsibilities before the remaining conversions. The initial 98-file
candidate count is therefore a lower bound, not a migration limit. Additional
candidates remain TODO until exact Node runs establish their assertions and setup
requirements. Any affected earlier owner is reopened with this dependency and
updated evidence rather than silently treated as already complete.

below are relative to the repository root; each owns its terminal receipt,
manifest, row results, resource observations and cleanup evidence.

Diagnostics were read with `make explain-run RESULTS_DIR=<exact root>
DETAIL=summary`, `DETAIL=fixtures` and `DETAIL=performance JSON=1` (exit 0).
RSS is an observed sweep subset and can count shared pages more than once; it is
not a complete process-tree peak. CPU samples are partial lower bounds, with
unavailable short-lived scopes; no zero-cost or performance win is inferred.
Existing diagnostics do not count individual credential derivations or S3 delete
requests. Those reductions require structural accounting and focused assertions,
not invented measurements. The browser baseline includes cold build work and is
not a controlled latency comparison. Future timing comparisons must state cache,
build, selection, source and host differences.

Confirmed correctness gaps: S3 pagination can stop at a duplicate token without
proving traversal complete; successful deletion is not followed by an empty-state
proof; failed package-bucket reset lacks permanent exclusion from reuse.
Confirmed unnecessary work: one Vitest coordinator per compatible file, jsdom
for pure reference/surface assertions, derivation for unused actor passwords,
and dedicated clones for proven StartStore-only selections. Cohort sharing and
remaining capability reductions are proof-gated optimizations.

Pinned Vitest 4.1.4 exposes public `createVitest`, `createSpecification` with
per-specification `testNamePattern`, `runTestSpecifications`, and reporter
module-completion hooks. The existing config has separate Node/jsdom projects;
file isolation and one worker must remain explicit in R08. Current browser
fixtures give fresh contexts the same worker-admin storage state; distinct
record IDs alone cannot justify sharing that actor. S3's pinned SDK exposes
`DeleteObjects` (at most 1,000 keys); per-object errors must be checked separately
from transport success. R05 must prove behavior against pinned SeaweedFS, including
multi-page deletion and mutation readiness, before retaining batching.

subsets are admitted. `retain` preserves the traced boundary, not a claim that
all helpers in the package require it. `review` is an open candidate requiring
owner proof, never a terminal disposition. Existing transaction selections remain
transaction-backed unless R01 proves a pure subset. Filesystem-only effects do
not require the managed object-store service.

mixed consumers: R03 must still inspect eligible call sites rather than treating
a password-taking API as proof that every caller needs hashing.

## Historical audit boundary

Sections 1–5 below retain the original static audit and its delivery record.
References to future authorization, deferred checks and the original seven-slice
scope are historical. Execution control and subsequent workstream records above
supersede those delivery instructions; normative owners remain authoritative.

## 1. Objective, authority, and evidence limits

Reduce actual test execution work, elapsed time, and resource consumption while
preserving production functionality, correctness, stability, and regression
detection. Preserve deterministic, independently attributable outcomes and
meaningful integration and end-to-end coverage.

The adopted [Testing Harness NLSpec](../testing-harness-nlspec.md) and applicable
product owners remain authoritative. This document is human guidance, not a new
requirements owner, conformance result, release result, or performance claim.
Tests, generators, runtime metadata, conformance, and release evidence must never
read, stat, hash, or otherwise depend on this document or other Markdown.

The audit used static source, configuration, catalog, and specification inspection
only. No tests, builds, benchmarks, or service operations were performed. Findings
identify repeated work and candidate improvements; they do not establish measured
cost, runtime correctness, safe additional sharing, or a quantified speedup.
Inspection was targeted rather than an assertion-by-assertion review of the full
suite. Runtime measurements and isolation characterization remain prerequisites
where specified below.

Related work: [Test Harness Resource Lifecycle Remediation](test-harness-resource-lifecycle-remediation.md).
That handoff records earlier lifecycle and suite/lane changes. Its historical test
passes do not qualify this proposal or a later source state. Reuse its implemented
ownership mechanisms; do not repeat completed changes or reopen its deferred
decisions without the evidence and authority required here.

## 2. Source posture and current architecture

Original audit date: 2026-10-18. Original source posture: `808203eaf` plus concurrent
uncommitted changes. Another chat was performing development during inspection.

Delivery recheck on 2026-10-18 observed HEAD `e98e1ec97`. Targeted inspection
reconfirmed the inventory counts, capacity defaults, and source anchors used below.
This is not a frozen whole-tree snapshot or a replay of every original inspection.
Revalidate affected source and governing requirements before future implementation;
preserve unrelated and concurrent changes.

### Inventory snapshot

| Runner | Active catalog rows | Relevant execution structure |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Go | 966 | 187 packages; compatible process grouping already exists |
| Vitest | 751 | 443 distinct files; 404 use the jsdom project |
| Playwright | 586 | 178 groups across six primary stages |
| Shell | 28 | Registered harness operations |

The 2,331 active rows were counted from the [test-family manifests](../../tools/test_families).
A row can select multiple tests. These are inspection counts, not permanent
completeness requirements, database creation counts, or the contents of one
aggregate invocation. Cache hits and exact selection affect executed work.

| Primary browser stage | Groups | Single-row groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Functional/webserver-backed | 73 | 22 |
| Support | 5 | 1 |
| Stateful | 17 | 12 |
| Measurement | 33 | 33 |
| Accessibility | 6 | 2 |
| Visual | 44 | 44 |

These counts come from the [browser batch manifest](../../tools/browser_e2e_batch_manifest.json).
Its alternate resettable/isolated selections must not be added to the six primary
stages as additional coverage. Selection resolves each requested row once.

### Existing foundations to preserve

- One [native suite owner](../../internal/testutil/harnessfixtures/production_linux.go)
  supplies compatible PostgreSQL and object-store consumers. Ordinary
  [PostgreSQL](../../internal/testutil/pgtest/pgtest.go) and
  [object-store](../../internal/testutil/s3test/s3test.go) helpers attach explicitly
  rather than silently creating another service.
- PostgreSQL uses immutable migrated templates, dedicated clones, and explicitly
  approved rollback fixtures. [Clone finalization](../../internal/testutil/pgtest/provisioning.go)
  establishes database-specific grants without replaying cluster provisioning.
- The [renderer owner](../../internal/testutil/harnessfixtures/renderer_linux.go)
  pools compatible infrastructure within an invocation. Chromium remains
  connection-owned; [test fixtures](../../apps/web/e2e/fixtures.ts) create fresh
  browser contexts. Container reuse does not eliminate every browser startup.
- The [graph compiler](../../tools/harness/scheduler/work-graph/compiler.mjs)
  already groups compatible Go rows and compatible same-file Vitest rows.
- The [topology](../../tools/execution_topology_manifest.json) owns a browser-lane
  default of four and maximum of six, subject to host admission. The
  [resource registry](../../tools/scheduler_resource_registry.json) now declares
  ceilings of 16 PostgreSQL tokens, eight object-store tokens, and 32 port lanes,
  with their host-derived bounds. These are admission budgets, not measured usage
  or a throughput guarantee. Earlier limits of eight/three/16 are superseded.
- Fifty-eight rows use `explicit_only`, including all 44 visual rows. Aggregate
  success does not establish that omitted rows passed. Excluding work from a gate
  must not be represented as making equivalent coverage cheaper.

## 3. Structural decisions and prioritized workstreams

### Design dispositions

1. Extend the existing scheduler, fixture owner, and runner adapters. Introduce no
   second resource manager, selection registry, scheduler, or resident test daemon.
2. Keep one authoritative policy for each lifecycle decision. Separate physical
   infrastructure ownership from test-state isolation and evidence attribution.
3. Remove replaced mechanisms during an approved cutover. Do not retain aliases,
   fallback runners, parallel implementations, or compatibility switches without
   a continuing requirement. Preserve public contracts until their owner approves
   an intentional replacement.
4. Carry features forward only when they materially improve the future subsystem.
   Reject cosmetic command rearrangement and complexity that does not remove
   demonstrated work or improve assurance.
5. Add an abstraction only when multiple real consumers need the same lifecycle
   contract. Prefer small explicit interfaces and enforceable ownership over
   per-test exceptions, global reset-hook collections, or growing allowlists.
6. Preserve individual test identities and outcomes while sharing execution
   infrastructure. Do not replace independent scenarios with one order-dependent
   test merely to reduce startup counts.
7. Retain an optimization only when its benefit is supported and its maintenance
   cost is proportionate. Do not weaken sampling, retries, security, cleanup, or
   coverage obligations to obtain a faster result.

### Priorities and readiness

Benefit rankings are hypotheses about opportunity, not a measured ordering of
current bottlenecks. Readiness does not grant implementation authorization.

| ID | Workstream and chosen direction | Expected benefit / complexity / reliability risk | Readiness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R01 | Move proven pure tests into the existing Node project; separate pure symbols from service-backed selections | Moderate / low / low | Ready for scoped implementation planning |
| R02 | Replace unnecessarily fragmented browser execution with bounded compatible cohorts | High potential / high / medium–high | Requires isolation characterization and owner amendment |
| R03 | Separate non-authentication actor preparation from credential behavior under test | Moderate–high potential / medium / medium | Requires measured attribution and owner review |
| R04 | Assign rollback transactions to additional proven store-only tests; split mixed rows first | Moderate potential / medium / high if misclassified | Requires per-row connection and state analysis |
| R05 | Replace serial object deletion with provider-supported batch deletion | Workload-dependent / medium / medium | Requires provider capability and failure-semantics validation |
| R06 | Refine scheduling costs and resource claims using existing retained diagnostics | Throughput-dependent / medium / medium | Requires compatible runtime observations |
| R07 | Consolidate redundant assertions only with named surviving coverage | Unproven / variable / high for broad deletion | No expensive-test deletion currently justified |

### R01 — Match execution environments to assertions

The [Vitest adapter](../../tools/harness/execution/runners/vitest.mjs) starts a fresh
runner for each compatible file selection. An uncached selection covering all 443
files therefore requires at least 443 invocations; incompatible contexts can split
one file further. The [Vite test configuration](../../apps/web/vite.config.ts)
adds jsdom and DOM setup to the browser-unit project.

The [reference-contract tests](../../packages/view-contracts/src/references.test.ts)
and [surface-contract tests](../../packages/view-contracts/src/surfaces.test.ts)
are concrete Node-project candidates: the inspected assertions exercise registry
data and object identity without DOM operations. Revalidate their import closure,
then use the existing `*.node.test.ts` convention and matching catalog projection.
Preserve assertions and exact selection. Consolidate small related pure files only
where they form a coherent suite and reduce actual invocation count.

The Workbook row
`module.workbook.catalog.communications_log_handoff_status_review_and_les_63b0f44db8`
in its [family manifest](../../tools/test_families/module.workbook.json) combines ten
symbols under PostgreSQL and object-store dependencies. The
[artifact-filter test](../../internal/modules/workbook/catalog_artifact_surface_test.go)
is pure registry inspection. Split that selection from the backed symbols.
This removes unnecessary services for the pure selection; it does not eliminate
services from an aggregate that still needs the remaining tests.

### R02 — Make browser cohorts reflect isolation and setup cost

The [manifest generator](../../tools/harness/generated-artifacts/execution-topology.mjs)
partitions visual work by row: all 44 visual groups select the same source file.
Twenty-two functional groups also contain only one catalog row. Each group incurs
a [Playwright invocation](../../tools/harness/browser/browser-catalog-group-cli.mjs)
and [global readiness/authentication setup](../../apps/web/e2e/global-setup.ts).

The [browser graph](../../tools/harness/scheduler/work-graph/browser.mjs) inserts
resets between selected groups on an affinity chain. The
[backend reset implementation](../../tools/harness/browser/start-web-e2e.sh),
`reset_session_backend`, stops the backend, resets persistent state, clears
Playwright state, and starts a replacement backend while retaining the frontend.
Selecting all 73 functional groups with four planned lanes implies 69 between-group
reset boundaries. Renderer pooling alone does not remove them.

Design bounded cohorts around proven compatible runtime profiles and state scope.
Keep fresh contexts, independently created mutable test data, exact selected
scenarios, and separate outcomes. Separate authentication administration, global
clock/fault mutation, incompatible profiles, and other shared-state consumers.
Do not assume every visual row can join one cohort.

Current TH-HARNESS-REQ-806 preserves existing group/reset boundaries. The
[manifest validator](../../tools/harness/browser/browser-batch-manifest.mjs) also
requires exactly one selector file per group. Change the adopted owner before
implementing a broader grouping contract. Preserve dedicated measurement
lifetimes, quiet intervals, and owner-defined sampling.

### R03 — Avoid repeatedly constructing unrelated credential fixtures

`SeedLocalUserRecord` in the [auth fixture helper](../../internal/modules/auth/testsupport/storetest/store.go)
derives a fresh production password hash for each actor. The
[password implementation](../../internal/platform/authn/password.go) uses 600,000
PBKDF2 iterations. [Workbook tests](../../internal/modules/workbook/coordination_surfaces_test.go)
repeat that preparation while testing query fields and collection behavior.

Measure its contribution before changing fixture APIs. Evaluate an owner-approved
immutable prepared credential input for non-authentication actor fixtures while
creating independent user rows for every test. Preserve real derivation, login,
credential changes, capacity behavior, and security assertions in their owning
tests. Do not reduce production hashing parameters or share mutable user records
or authenticated sessions across unrelated tests.

### R04 — Use the least expensive proved database capability

The catalog declares 94 transaction rows, 312 dedicated-database rows, and 11
migration-capability rows. These are not database creation counts or a complete
count of individual migration scenarios.

`BeginRollbackDBT` in [pgtest](../../internal/testutil/pgtest/pgtest.go) reuses a
database by caller package within a process, serializes borrowers, and starts a
fresh transaction. Settlement rolls back, closes the connection, and poisons the
fixture after uncertain cleanup. The
[fixture policy registry](../../tools/postgres_fixture_policy_registry.json)
explicitly admits transaction rows.

Trace all database access and external effects before converting a dedicated row.
Split mixed rows first. Prove that no connection escapes the rollback boundary and
that no assertion requires committed-state observation. Retain real dedicated and
migration isolation where required. Compare reduced clone/drop work against the
serialization imposed by the shared fixture mutex.

### R05 — Reduce object-store cleanup round trips

`cleanupPrefix` in [s3test](../../internal/testutil/s3test/s3test.go) paginates objects
and issues serial `DeleteObject` requests. `PreparePackageBucketT` retains exclusive
package-bucket ownership and empties it before the next borrower.

Prefer the provider's batch-delete operation if its supported semantics satisfy
the existing cleanup contract. Prove partial-failure reporting, pagination
completeness, cancellation behavior, and empty-state verification. If the provider
cannot support that contract, defer R05 rather than adding a compatibility fallback
or weakening cleanup. Preserve exact bucket/prefix ownership; never sweep another
concurrent consumer's data. Prefix isolation is sufficient only when every relevant
operation respects that prefix.

### R06 — Tune coordination after removing unnecessary work

The [work-graph owner](../../tools/harness_work_graph_owner.json) supplies coarse
evidence-class estimates. Browser planning sums row estimates despite varying
scenario counts and setup costs. [Go grouping](../../tools/harness/backend/go-lpt-shards.mjs)
assigns process CPU budgets; transaction and package-bucket fixtures can serialize
work inside admitted processes.

Use compatible retained observations to distinguish startup, fixture preparation,
test execution, cleanup, and admission wait. Assess cohort balance, actual child
parallelism, and renderer retirement/reacquisition around quiet measurement work.
Keep resource claims consistent with observed peak envelopes, resident ownership,
and cleanup headroom. Do not raise limits again as a substitute for removing work.
Amend the owner if changing its estimate or scheduling model. Do not introduce a
new measurement daemon, benchmark baseline, or publication gate.

### R07 — Preserve assurance when consolidating coverage

The original static inventory found no duplicate exact Go, Vitest, or Playwright
selector mappings. This does not prove semantic uniqueness or constitute a
successful canonical catalog check.

The [surface-contract tests](../../packages/view-contracts/src/surfaces.test.ts)
repeat the same `requiredReferencePackKeys` equality assertion in two tests. That
is a concrete consolidation candidate with negligible expected performance benefit.
No expensive test deletion is justified by the present evidence.

Before retiring coverage, map the required behavior, stimulus, observation,
execution layer, fixture, evidence context, and failure modes to named surviving
coverage. Store, HTTP, browser, visual, and accessibility assertions can detect
different regressions even when their subject overlaps. Prefer removing duplicated
preparation before removing assertions.

Persistent cross-file Vitest processes remain deferred: TH-HARNESS-REQ-805 currently
prohibits them. First exploit the existing Node project and coherent same-file
grouping. Do not introduce a resident test daemon or an alternate execution path.

## 4. Isolation, authority, and interface boundaries

| Resource | Permitted sharing direction | Boundary to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL service | Compatible invocation-wide generation | Separate physical service for cluster-global mutation |
| Migrated template | Immutable shared source | Independent dedicated databases for committed-state behavior |
| Rollback fixture | Approved package/process reuse | Fresh transaction, no escaped connections, poisoning after uncertain cleanup |
| Object-store service | Shared physical service | Exclusive bucket or fully enforced namespace |
| Renderer container/server | Existing compatible pool | Exclusive borrow and proven settlement |
| Browser context | Fresh per test | Independent cookies, storage, routing, permissions, and pages |
| Application stack | Compatible cohort/lane | Required process replacement and persistent-state reset |
| Prepared fixture | Immutable input or snapshot | Independent mutable records or clones |
| Measurement infrastructure | Shared immutable preparation where permitted | Dedicated lifetime, quiet interval, and owner-defined sampling |

Preserve dedicated isolation for cross-connection visibility, concurrency races,
background workers, WebSockets, recovery, migration paths, and database identity.
A migrated template cannot prove an upgrade path. Do not replace real migration
execution with current-schema inspection.

Unique incident or record IDs alone do not establish independence. Cohort admission
must account for user preferences, session limits, global controls, background
activity, shared listings, and cleanup scope. Sharing physical infrastructure must
not create a shared mutable baseline or order dependency.

No production API or database migration is proposed. Catalog, grouping, schema,
and evidence-contract changes must update their authoritative owners and generated
projections together. Do not hand-edit generated outputs. Existing row identities
and failure semantics remain unless an owner-backed replacement mapping explicitly
changes them. Historical evidence stays historical; no translation layer makes it
qualify changed contracts.

## 5. Implementation sequence and acceptance

### Ordered future work

1. Revalidate the baseline and reconcile concurrent lifecycle changes. Inspect
   applicable instruction chains, source, and owners before editing. Establish
   exact equal-coverage selections and cache conditions; do not treat reduced
   aggregate scope as improved execution efficiency.
2. Implement R01 first after separate implementation authorization. Preserve the
   selector union and assertions while removing unnecessary jsdom and managed
   services from eligible selections.
3. Attribute remaining costs using existing exact-run diagnostics. Observe runner
   and browser starts, backend restarts, clone/drop counts, fixture construction,
   cleanup, queue time, CPU time, peak memory, and resource residue. Count shared
   physical costs once, distinguish cold and warm conditions, and union overlapping
   intervals rather than summing them into wall time.
4. Develop R02–R05 as separate bounded slices. Each slice needs its isolation proof,
   applicable adopted owner change, and a named validation selection before
   implementation. Preserve current behavior when these prerequisites are absent.
5. Tune scheduling last using the reduced workload and observed costs. Retain
   resident accounting, cleanup headroom, and exclusive measurement admission.
   Revisit R07 only when named replacement coverage is demonstrated.

### Acceptance for each implemented slice

- Every selected test has exactly one independently attributable outcome; partial
  selection executes no additional cases, and missing or skipped outcomes cannot
  pass.
- Affected tests pass alone and in reordered compatible selections. Shared setup
  does not turn a failed predecessor into an unaccounted or misleading successor.
- Concurrent consumers cannot observe or clean another test's state.
- Partial startup, cancellation, cleanup failure, and owner loss preserve primary
  failure attribution, cleanup ownership, quarantine, and independently completed
  evidence. Product retries do not hide failures.
- Required functionality, integration paths, migration behavior, security checks,
  and measurement semantics remain covered. Visual and accessibility observations
  remain distinct from product-behavior and publication obligations.
- The intended mechanism removes demonstrated work. Report structural changes
  such as fewer launches separately from measured wall-time/resource changes;
  claim only improvements supported by comparable observations.
- Replaced code paths are removed. No unnecessary compatibility mechanism or new
  policy owner remains behind.

### Verification and handoff obligations

Future implementation uses public Make targets from the repository root and
`make task-guide OWNER=<owner-id>` to select narrow verification. Diagnose failures
before retrying or broadening. Run `make agent-finalize` before broader end-of-run
implementation checks; it can rewrite generated artifacts. Verify applicable
generated/schema projections through their public Make checks.

Select Visual/UI-review evidence explicitly when affected; aggregate success does
not include those excluded rows. Report exact source identity, commands,
selections, run roots, process exits, cleanup outcomes, and skipped checks. Provide
`RESULTS_DIR` only for a compatible successful full warm check; otherwise report
retained-run maintenance skipped. Do not create an extra warm run merely to supply
that input.

### Documentation delivery record

This delivery creates only this planning handoff. It performs no product
verification, generation, formatting, finalization, benchmark, service operation,
or harness implementation. Inspection used read-only Git queries, bounded source
reads/searches, and in-memory JSON inventory counts.

`make lint-markdown` is deferred under the user's continuing noninterference
restriction. Its omission is explicit; no canonical documentation-check pass is
claimed. Product tests and `agent-finalize` are inapplicable to this documentation
delivery and were not run. The implementation sequence above describes future
authorized work, not actions performed to create this file.

## R02.foundation completion and owner admission record

**Status: DONE.** The foundation closes before the first owner onboarding slice. All 586 catalog rows were resolved to their exact static test bodies (including constant/array-index titles), hooks, imported helper functions and used classes. Import/identifier closure was supplemented by inspection of global runtime fault routes, custom fixtures, measurement overrides, directory/administration pages and module-level mutable state. Filenames and unique record IDs were not used as sharing authority. The per-row proposed scopes below remain subject to each owner slice; the authored catalog still admits only singletons and dedicated measurement at this boundary.

Adopted REQ-806 projects through family manifest **v11**, topology **v15**, and browser batch manifest **v13**. Superseded schema files/readers were removed; generated validators and embedded metadata came from Make. Catalog `browser_state_scope` is required only for Playwright and distinguishes `test_owned`, `isolated`, and `measurement`. Generated groups now describe compatibility partitions, preserving owner/project/configuration, runtime/trust, resource, service/fixture, stage and state scope. Compiler selection precedes deterministic bounded packing; exact selectors and policy bind cohort identities. The existing published graph transports row bindings; the joined row-list environment path and old single-selector-file helper were removed. Public Make commands and semantic row identities are unchanged.

Every observed browser actor/session is now a test-scoped `testActor`, with `testActorPage` and `testActorRequest` replacing the old worker fixture names without aliases. A private worker provisioning account only creates actors and revokes/verifies owned sessions. Each actor is an independent record with ephemeral credentials created/login-verified through real public workflows. No production credential policy or API changed. Test contexts, routes, requests and secondary sessions retain their existing owned teardown. The visual investigation map clears in its verification `finally`; page-indexed WeakMaps and WeakSets cannot transfer state to a new context; the query observer hook drains only its page. Measurement overrides and quiet lifetimes remain dedicated.

The public Playwright Reporter checkpoints canonical row outcomes after test fixtures and applicable suite hooks settle. Anchored bounded reads and atomic row publication preserve completed work through coordinator loss. A test failure stops the cohort (`maxFailures=1`, zero retries); unexecuted rows are explicit `skipped_dependency`, while interrupted missing work is `cancelled`. Worker or global teardown errors fail the cohort without rewriting independently settled test outcomes (scope corrected during R02.harness.browser). The pinned public failure-limit notification is recognized only by its exact message-only shape and an independently observed failure; it is not another runner failure. Failure/reset uncertainty uses the existing broker quarantine/reallocation path, with independent successors finalizable after failed resets. No new scheduler, resource manager, daemon or selection registry was introduced.

Costs now include exact selected test counts plus one startup/cleanup overhead per cohort. Browser coordinator/worker reservations are CPU 2, memory 640 MiB and 4 processes, separately from resident renderer/services. No ceiling or deadline increased. Final calibration belongs to R06. The real two-row visual foundation run passed with two coordinator launches and one reset, retaining the original singleton admission for comparison; it is not a batching speedup claim. Additional actor derivation/login work is an explicit isolation cost to include in final observations.

compatibility partitions by unchanged semantic row ID, within each stage. It
includes ordinary and aggregate routing stages. A partition may absorb members
from several old groups; execution still uses only the selected rows, packed
within the unchanged work-unit envelope. New runtime cohort IDs bind the full

### R06 calibration decisions and specification disposition

Adopted REQ-801 now names the work-graph owner's **v7** invocation/lifecycle
policy. Authored Go overhead is 5000 ms startup plus 250 ms settlement, charged
once per compatible process. Selected row estimates remain conservative and
additive: neither transaction mutexes nor package bucket locks become parallel
merely because GOMAXPROCS is greater than one. Existing CPU/worker budgets and
resource profiles remain unchanged. Vitest retains 1000/250 ms invocation
overhead and a single isolated file worker; its selected row estimates still
include file setup/teardown. Browser topology retains 4000/2000 ms overhead per
cohort and exact-title selected costs.

The same existing work-graph owner now declares formerly hard-coded lifecycle
estimates: browser reset 4000 ms (was 1000), target finalization 500 ms,
measurement finalization 500 ms, and immutable fixture preparation 120000 ms.
The latter three are retained conservative estimates, not new measurements.
Reset is charged only by its separate unit; no borrower adds it again. Broker
acquisition/release diagnostics remain separate from selected test durations;
resident allocation accounting and cleanup headroom are unchanged. There is no
new scheduler, policy registry, live adaptation, deadline or resource ceiling.
The superseded v6 schema/validator readers are removed at coordinated generation.
Row identities are unchanged; work-unit semantic/graph digests change with costs.
Historical plans remain historical.

The specification's older stateful-execution paragraph still mentioned
selector-file resets. It now explicitly delegates direct and scheduled boundaries
to REQ-806's selected cohorts; this removes a stale contradictory restatement,
without changing the already implemented/adopted R02 behavior.

Calibration evidence uses exact retained public terminal artifacts, never Markdown
inputs. Cache-off means harness cache disabled; language/build caches may be warm.
These observations qualify component estimates, not a controlled speedup claim:

| Run / source selection | Observation | Decision / limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remediation01-r04-module-workbook-ordered`, exact three-row crosswalk union recorded above | Go process wall minus selected test duration: 1299 ms service-free, 5199/5200 ms for dedicated/rollback selections | One 5250 ms Go invocation allowance covers this observed process overhead; do not multiply it per row or divide serialized row work by CPU |
| `remediation01-r05-provider`, exact two provider rows recorded above | Go overhead 5066/5046 ms | Corroborates conservative Go allowance after batch cleanup; fixture/test work remains in selected durations |
| `remediation01-r08-node-final` and `remediation01-r08-dom-final` | Two-file coordinator units 1338/2161 ms; selected test sums 6/89 ms | Retain conservative Vitest startup/cleanup and per-row estimates; insufficient data to narrow broad unit costs or claim complete process peaks |
| `remediation01-r02-visual-ordinary-one` | 18 resets: 3319–3551 ms; normal group wall minus selected duration approximately 5430–6109 ms; first allocation groups approximately 18308–19943 ms; summary units 85/198 ms | Reset estimate becomes 4000 ms; retain six-second cohort overhead. parallel policy owner is introduced. This closes the previously implicit
first/last allocation allowance without double-counting reset units.

### Maintainer interface and lifecycle summary

- **Selection and capability:** public Make commands and `make task-guide` remain
  the entry points. Authored family/catalog inputs own semantic rows, exact
  selectors, capabilities and browser state scopes. The existing Node filename
  convention is the only environment declaration; no per-file environment map or
  second selection registry exists. Regenerate projections through Make. Mixed
  Go rows have explicit crosswalks above; unchanged claims retain their row IDs.
- **Actor construction:** Auth's test-support `SeedActor` accepts attributes,
  including optional fixed identity for ordering assertions. Its internal
  `sync.OnceValues` prepares one immutable credential with the production hash
  implementation and random test-only input; every seed creates an independent
  user. Password-taking helpers remain for authentication behavior and capacity.
  Browser actors are independently created and logged in through real public
  workflows; the worker provisioning account is private control-plane setup only.
- **Database isolation:** admitted store-only tests use `StartStore` and
  `BeginRollbackDBT` through the existing fixture-policy registry. Transaction
  scopes and package mutexes remain serial; close/rollback uncertainty permanently
  poisons the generation. Dedicated databases remain for cross-connection, commit,
  concurrency, background, recovery, identity and migration assertions.
- **Object cleanup:** harness-only S3 cleanup batches at most 1000 keys, checks
  transport and object errors, rejects malformed/repeated continuation state, and
  independently proves the exact namespace empty. Reusable buckets must also
  prove mutation readiness. Missing destruction targets do not prove reusable
  admission; uncertain creation retains exact cleanup reservation. No production
  storage API was widened and no serial/batch compatibility branch remains.
- **Vitest lifetime:** compatible exact project/file/title selections share a fresh
  bounded coordinator with one isolated file worker. Public TestSpecification
  filters remain per file. Public worker-stop acknowledgement and physical exit
  precede settlement. Canonical row checkpoints preserve independently completed
  files through interruption; suite errors stay file-scoped and runner errors
  remain invocation-scoped. There is no resident daemon or old single-file path.
- **Browser lifetime:** generated groups are compatibility partitions. Select rows
  first, pack deterministically, then assign compatible cohorts to existing lanes.
  Context, actor/session and mutable records are test-owned; incompatible global
  consumers remain singleton. Resets separate successive cohorts on a lane.
  Failure/uncertain reset quarantines the allocation; independent work can acquire
  a clean allocation without retrying product work. Completed outcomes survive.
  Measurements keep dedicated lifetimes, quiet admission and finalization; visual
  update remains exclusive and ordinary visual rows remain explicit-only.
  Native clipboard consumers establish their own copied/written contents; a fresh
  browser context alone does not prove clipboard isolation. Timeline Create
  suppresses non-primary mouse-release defaults before they can paste into the
  focused authoring control. Primary and keyboard activation remain unchanged.
- **Cost and admission:** the existing work-graph owner v7 contains Go/Vitest
  invocation policy and lifecycle estimates; browser topology owns its cohort
  invocation overhead. Startup/settlement and first/last allocation boundaries are
  charged once, reset units separately, and serialized rows are never divided by
  CPU count. Packing reserves allocation headroom within unchanged envelopes.
  Resource ceilings, resident accounting, cleanup admission and measurement
  exclusivity remain owned by the existing scheduler/broker.
- **Current contracts:** family v11, topology v15, browser batch v13, work-graph
  owner v7, Vitest request/reports v1 and failure details v3, service journal/ledger
  v2. Browser group result v9 and target result v7 retain canonical evidence. Old
  schema readers/writers and selector-file aliases are removed; historical runs
  are not translated into current qualification. Exact schema/group/row crosswalks
  are above.
- **Future verification:** select narrow registered rows, retain a fresh run ID and
  the owning process exit, inspect the exact public run artifacts, and diagnose
  before rerunning. `agent-finalize` precedes broad end-of-run checks. Explicitly
  select visual rows and relevant measurement lifetimes; aggregate success is not

### V00 checkpoint/drop diagnostic follow-up — physical cause unresolved

The follow-up investigation re-read the exact final-CI summary, the three failed
row artifacts, the bounded PostgreSQL regression log and published resource
observations. No product test was rerun, service restarted, runtime configuration
changed or implementation edited. V00 remains **BLOCKED**; this is diagnostic
evidence, not a completed repair workstream or a root-cause closure.

The pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 implementation establishes the mechanism:

- Both ordinary and forced database drops discard target buffers and request an
  immediate, forced, synchronous checkpoint before removing database files.
  `FORCE` changes connection termination; it does not bypass the checkpoint.
  See [18.6 database commands](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/commands/dbcommands.c#L1867).
- A checkpoint request must observe a checkpoint starting after its request and
  then completing. If another checkpoint is already running, waiting for its
  completion alone is insufficient. This explains the observed
  `CheckpointStart` and `CheckpointDone` states. See
  [18.6 checkpointer coordination](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/postmaster/checkpointer.c#L72).
- `DataFileSync` wraps the relation-file synchronization call. A sampled wait
  establishes that operation, but cannot distinguish one long synchronization
  from many shorter ones between observations. See
  [18.6 relation-file synchronization](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/storage/smgr/md.c#L1894).

The current harness adds a plausible amplification path that needs separate
characterization. `internal/testutil/postgrescleanup/forced_drop.go` escalates
either SQLSTATE 55006 or an ordinary deadline into a fresh forced operation.
The pgtest budgets are five seconds ordinary and fifteen seconds forced. If the
ordinary drop expired while waiting for a checkpoint, resubmitting the forced
drop can request another checkpoint while the earlier checkpoint continues.
This is a source-proved possibility, not proof that it caused all three retained
failures. The final return discards the ordinary error/observation after fallback,
so the retained forced-only diagnostic cannot establish that first attempt's
wait. Preserve both attempt observations in any diagnostic repair.

The four-database regression failed four independent targets with the same
checkpoint counters, 513 requested / 512 done, while reporting no lock blockers.
The Jobs counter advanced during its forced wait. These observations establish a
shared checkpoint dependency and some progress; they do not prove a deadlock,
continuous I/O stall, storage-device fault or inadequate scheduler capacity.
Target-specific catalog admission cannot make PostgreSQL's checkpoint local to
one database. A global harness lock is not justified by this evidence either.

Read-only environment inspection reported Docker Desktop on the WSL2 kernel.
The exact pinned image declares a volume at `/var/lib/postgresql`; the authored
container request places PGDATA at `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker` without a
replacement mount or tmpfs. The separate harness scratch-root setting only
places the TLS/runtime files in this startup path. Consequently the earlier
measurement fixture's `/tmp` capacity failure is not evidence of PostgreSQL data
volume exhaustion. Docker's reported overlayfs driver does not establish that
the PostgreSQL volume uses the container writable layer. The removed CI
container's backing device, individual fsync latencies and checkpoint log
timings were not retained and are not inferred from current host configuration.

  before proof revocation/teardown. A logical suite Close callback is too late

### PG06 follow-up — checkpoint backlog and reset work source

The user requested root-cause investigation after the aggregate recurrence.
Read-only analysis of the exact failed run and PostgreSQL REL_18_6 source
identifies the following causal chain; no new test or environment operation was
launched for this investigation. The already authorized measurement invocation
continues independently on unchanged source.

1. Both Recovery database drops obtained admission in 11–12ms, after all owned
   connections stopped. Their samples show zero blockers, CheckpointStart then
   CheckpointDone, and a checkpointer doing DataFileSync. Their operation budgets
   expire at 20000ms. This establishes a shared checkpoint barrier as the direct
   cause, rather than target-lock contention, a surviving owned connection, or
   a retry that no longer exists.
2. The completed checkpoint synchronized 54768 files in 17575ms; the longest
   individual synchronization was 36ms. PostgreSQL's sync loop visits pending
   files serially. The evidence shows aggregate file work, not one 17-second
   fsync. The following recorded checkpoint synchronized another 2291 files in
   4264ms. A drop must observe a checkpoint starting after its request, so
   waiting behind an existing checkpoint can span more than one checkpoint.
3. There is a concrete source of avoidable file work in
   `internal/platform/harnessruntime/reset.go`: resetAdmittedDatabase inventories
   every mutable public table and truncateTables unconditionally issues one
   TRUNCATE TABLE … CASCADE for the whole inventory. CI retained 113 completed
   resets, each covering all 144 mutable tables: 16272 table truncations before
   counting TOAST tables or rebuilt indexes. The public unit-event stream records
   61 completed resets in graph interval 1900000–2300000ms.
4. PostgreSQL transaction-safe TRUNCATE replaces each table/TOAST storage file
   and rebuilds its indexes. mdcreate registers even a newly created empty
   permanent file for synchronization. Commit-time removal retains the old main
   fork, truncated to zero, until checkpoint unlink processing; an unlink request
   does not itself cancel an existing sync request. Repeating this on empty
   tables therefore creates pending file work even when the reset's SQL is fast.
   The shared service makes that work visible to an unrelated database drop.

Primary-source anchors (pinned version):

- [drop checkpoint barrier](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/commands/dbcommands.c#L1735)
- [request start/completion protocol](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/postmaster/checkpointer.c#L65)
- [TRUNCATE file replacement and index rebuild](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/commands/tablecmds.c#L2097)
- [new-file sync registration and deferred main-fork deletion](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/storage/smgr/md.c#L246)
- [serial sync loop and separate unlink queue](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_6/src/backend/storage/sync/sync.c#L339)

The confirmed failure mechanism is unbounded shared checkpoint work meeting a
fixed per-drop deadline. Full-schema reset is a source-proved contributor to
that work. The retained numeric projection intentionally contains no per-file
paths/database attribution; it cannot prove that every one of the 54768 files
originated in those 61 resets or quantify the exact contribution of clones and
other writes. Its service clock must not be equated with the graph clock.
A faulty device, Docker mount, or one slow fsync remains unproved. The 58634ms
checkpoint write interval may include PostgreSQL pacing; it is not a measured
device-write latency. Immediate requests suppress further pacing, but do not
bypass the currently running sync loop or the required later checkpoint.

Remediation direction now belongs first to harness reset/cluster-isolation
design: eliminate unnecessary relation-file replacement, and make cluster-wide
maintenance interference explicit for lifecycle-sensitive selections. Prove
any replacement preserves complete reset, FK/trigger/sequence semantics,
bootstrap state and failed-reuse exclusion. A blind storage relocation, global
lock, extra checkpoint, or deadline increase is not established by this evidence.
PG06/V00 remain blocked on an accepted, validated correction; this causal
refinement does not convert failed CI into success.

approximately 982 pending file synchronizations per reset at this schema. The
zero-reset control has none. No volume change or concurrent broad invocation is
needed to create a backlog larger than the 54768-file checkpoint in failed CI.
The exact per-file attribution of the historical CI checkpoint remains absent,
but reset-generated deferred synchronization is now causally demonstrated,
rather than merely inferred from simultaneous activity. Timing remains specific
to these runs and is not a universal per-reset performance guarantee.

The diagnostic also sampled per-database directory counts, but normal passing
Go output was not retained by the existing collector, so its t.Log messages are
absent from published unit logs. Those unretained count values are not claimed
as evidence. The checkpoint artifact independently supplies the stronger
retained synchronization counts above; no rerun was performed to recover logs.
The temporary instrumentation patch and checksum record remain at
`/tmp/cartulary-reset-probe.patch` and
`/tmp/cartulary-reset-probe.identity.json` for local investigation; these are not
new acceptance-artifact contracts or executable policy inputs.

The instrumented file identity
`294524270b5b09ecda4d74906f00200d048ddb9807e8609e6beb7c18557377d3`
was checked before restoring the original file, which again matches
`3fca8a70ef2e5d9a40fb865db05e62c1515c903c68472849292046049b4c5734`.
No production or permanent test change was added by this comparison. Existing
assertions, including reset metadata/bootstrap correctness and contention
classification, all passed.

**Root cause at the harness boundary:** full-schema TRUNCATE resets report
logical completion while leaving substantial physical synchronization/unlink
work on the shared PostgreSQL service. A later drop must cross the cluster-wide
checkpoint barrier, so its bounded operation inherits work from unrelated
completed resets. In CI, both Recovery drops reached that barrier promptly,
waited through an existing checkpoint into a subsequent one, and exhausted
their 20-second caps. The former fallback was an amplifier; removing it did
not remove this deferred-work coupling. The data does not establish a faulty
physical device, Docker volume, or one multi-second fsync.

PG06's investigation is complete for this mechanism; its repair acceptance
remains BLOCKED. The durable follow-on correction must bound/eliminate reset
file churn and address shared-cluster interference for lifecycle-sensitive
selections, with complete reset and cleanup semantics preserved. A blind
timeout increase, global lock, extra checkpoint or storage relocation is not
the accepted correction. This completion is recorded before PG07's final
source-identity and documentation checks.

### PG06.R01 completion — transactional clearing

Reset now validates the complete Recovery catalog before mutation, snapshots
all protected metadata contents, locks mutable tables deterministically, disables
ordinary replication triggers and rejects row-security filtering, deletes only
Recovery-writable rows, and invokes the existing owner algorithms for protected
claims. It proves every mutable table empty before restoring ordinary triggers
and bootstrap, checks all bootstrap/audit counts and absence of other state,
rechecks metadata and admission, and commits. No reset truncation, sequence
rewind, index rebuilding or relation replacement remains.

The existing 30-second database allowance reserves its final five seconds for
rollback/release. Unknown commit settlement stays unknown. Primary failures and
safe settlement failures are separately retained. Lost Recovery admission cannot
report successful release; an unreleased PostgreSQL session is discarded with a
cancelled close context, preventing an unbounded graceful-close wait. These
internal lifecycle changes add no grants, callbacks registry, retries or limits.

settlement-failure records. Old runs remain historical. Generated outputs were

use fresh databases for initialization and returned identities thereafter.

Status remains `IN_PROGRESS`; no dependent consumer workstream has begun.
All family rows were projected atomically to the required closed isolation field
so that schema adoption does not leave an executable partially migrated catalog.

owners keyed by shared scope, exclusive work unit, browser allocation, or a
measurement fixture. Native service bindings carry generation, provisioning and
template policy, isolation scope, and allocation identity. Browser admission now
requires the exclusive binding. Physical resources depend on their resident
claims and exact owner proof; failed cleanup retains those dependencies.

validation of these changes remains pending.

### PG06.C00 completion — cluster scope and physical ownership

Status `DONE`. R01 was complete before this work began; all C01 owner slices
remain `TODO` until their own acceptance. The Testing Harness replacement
contracts are projected by the existing catalog, topology, native fixture owner,
service helper, admission system and recovery graph. Human specification fidelity
review remains distinct from these automated checks.

- Explicit `none/shared/exclusive` scope is required for each catalog row and
  policy operation. PostgreSQL dependencies require compatible non-`none` scope
  before provisioning; browser and migration capabilities require exclusive
  scope. Scope partitions Go work units, browser cohorts, semantic digests and
  fixture reuse. Existing self-owned lifecycles keep their physical owner.
- The shared ordinary cluster, exclusive unit clusters, browser allocation
  clusters, and measurement builder/clone clusters use the same native owner.
  Physical service identity is independent of database identity. A PostgreSQL-only
  builder can later compose an object-store binding without reprovisioning.
- Exact validated binding proofs identify physical generation, template and
  provisioning policy, scope and owning allocation. Browser admission requires
  the exclusive proof. Ambient service credentials cannot select a generation.
  The public task guide exposes the declared scope.
- Resident memory, processes, ports and PostgreSQL claims are additive per
  actual cluster; the existing writable-volume capability is retained without
  inventing storage capacity. Impossible startup/self-blocking shapes reject
  before provisioning, cleanup headroom remains reserved, and final consumers
  retire completed generations. Self-owned selections do not reserve phantom
  broker services. Capacity ceilings are unchanged.
- PostgreSQL and object-store lifetimes are independent. Browser allocations
  save both dependencies and their cleanup environment, clear their exact bucket
  before releasing the object-store dependency, and retain database disposal at
  the owned cluster boundary. Failed cleanup quarantines reuse and preserves
  exact recovery proof. No product work is retried.

### Historical pre-C02 maintenance interface and lifecycle reference

- **Reset owner:** `internal/platform/harnessruntime/reset.go` performs one
  bounded transaction after the old backend, workers, listeners and connections
  have stopped and exclusive Recovery-target admission is held. Its injected
  Recovery catalog classifies every public table. Deterministic locks and
  transaction-local replication/row-security policy precede direct deletion and
  owner rebuilds. Every mutable table must be empty before bootstrap; bootstrap
  effects and protected metadata are checked exactly before admission recheck
  and commit. Rollback/admission release share bounded settlement allowance;
  primary and settlement failures remain distinct. Unknown settlement quarantines.
- **Derived state:** the shared Recovery PostgreSQL rebuild dispatcher owns
  Entities identifier claims and Parties key claims. Composition supplies the
  existing catalog and executor; the platform controller imports no domain owner.
  Unknown/protected classifications fail closed. No extra Recovery/runtime
  privilege, second registry, arbitrary SQL hook or reset-specific algorithm.
- **Reset compatibility:** generated identities advance. Tests use returned IDs;
  fresh databases own sequence-initialization assertions. Ordinary reset preserves
  relation storage identity and exact permitted migration/cryptographic metadata,
  including permitted absence. No truncation, sequence rewind, index rebuild,
  maintenance checkpoint or forced vacuum occurs in ordinary reset paths.
- **Cluster binding:** authored closed postgres_isolation is independent of
  database capability. Compatible ordinary rollback/committed tests use shared
  PostgreSQL; browser allocations, dedicated measurements and lifecycle-sensitive
  units use exclusive generations. A Recovery fixture may keep its related
  databases in its own generation. Existing self-owned tests reserve their real
  cluster without requesting an unused broker cluster. Exact generation, scope,
  allocation and provisioning/template policy bind attachments. Measurement
  attachment also binds its exact builder/profile/snapshot. No ambient rebinding.
- **Accounting and teardown:** existing admission charges startup activity and
  physical service residency separately. Residency persists while idle and until
  physical settlement; eligible idle allocations retire through existing cleanup.
  Each database settles before its cluster, each bucket before its object store,
  and renderer ownership remains independent. Failed publication, cancellation,
  owner loss or uncertain cleanup removes reuse eligibility and retains exact
  recovery proof. Shared host CPU/storage remain shared; exclusive clusters isolate
  PostgreSQL queues and control-plane state, not the physical device.
- **Evidence:** roster v2 identifies every active/retiring owned service.
  Checkpoint v2 collects before each cluster shuts down, with independent clocks,
  exact service generation and completeness. Drop diagnostics carry observed
  service generation or explicit null. Canonical dispatch/admission facts permit
  “not launched”; launched missing evidence and malformed present artifacts still
  fail. Performance explanation v5 preserves primary admission/startup/cleanup
  causes separately from unavailable derived summaries. Historical schemas are
  investigation evidence and have no current-reader compatibility aliases.
- **Scratch:** machine-cache/harness-scratch is the default, independent of
  TMPDIR; explicit external absolute override remains supported. Successful owners
  clean immediately. Bounded stale cleanup requires old private ownership proof,
  a proven-dead process and safe settlement; live, unknown, sealed-finalizing and
  unresolved owners retain their proof. There is no unscoped temp-directory sweep.
  The selected root still needs capacity for the fixture; no storage device move
  or database durability change is implied by moving disposable scratch.
- **Maintenance path:** edit authored catalog/topology/policy/schema inputs,
  regenerate through Make and validate exact owner selections before broader
  verification. Preserve public commands and unchanged semantic rows. The row,
  schema and group crosswalks above identify every cutover. This human tracker is
  never an executable policy source. Specification adoption follows the user's
  selected plan; automated checks do not substitute for human fidelity review.

Refined deterministic C03 setup: use the isolated test admission root's existing
kernel mutex to hold both host transitions after logical reservation. Observe
both stack pins under the broker mutex, then release the admission mutex. This
avoids relying on sleeps or renderer-reservation ordering. Both admitted requests
must complete within the existing bounded test context, reacquire through the
existing broker and settle their leases/host claims. The test may use the existing
fake physical provider; separate native lifecycle checks cover actual renderer
processes. A withdrawn request must yield its stack pin as well as its renderer
slot and rebuild resident references before the next admission attempt. Reserve
a renderer before pinning a stack so a request waiting for a logical renderer
cannot prevent idle-stack retirement. This design remains pending experimental

### Current maintenance interface and lifecycle reference (C02 cutover)

This reference supersedes the pre-C02 sharing description above. Acceptance remains
open while the exact final-source CI and explicit-only checks run.

- Reset performs one bounded transaction after the backend, connections, workers
  and listeners stop and exclusive Recovery-target admission is held. The existing
  Recovery catalog classifies all mutable/protected tables. Deterministic locks,
  transaction-local replication behavior and fail-closed row-security handling
  precede direct clearing and owner-controlled derived-claim rebuilding. Every
  mutable table must be empty before bootstrap; bootstrap effects including audit
  and protected metadata contents/allowed absence are verified before commit.
- Entities and Parties retain the existing Recovery rebuild algorithms and their
  privileges. Composition passes catalog and executor into the platform controller;
  no domain import, second registry, arbitrary SQL callback or extra grant exists.
  Sequences advance; fresh databases own initialization assertions. Ordinary reset
  never truncates, rewinds sequences, replaces relations, rebuilds indexes, forces
  a checkpoint or forces vacuum. The existing 30-second allowance reserves five
  seconds for bounded settlement; uncertain commit/rollback/release quarantines.
- Database capability and cluster scope remain separate, but compatibility covers
  the entire fixture lifecycle. Dedicated creation/drop and migration capabilities
  require exclusive clusters. Only approved transaction buckets may remain shared,
  with no per-test database replacement/drop and no cluster-lifecycle assertions.
  Browser allocations and measurements are exclusive; one Recovery fixture may
  share its own cluster among its related databases. Explicit self-owned fixtures
  retain their physical owner and are not duplicated by the broker.
- Registry v5 declares allowed cluster scopes; native validation rejects forbidden
  requests before provisioning. Attachments bind physical generation, scope,
  allocation and provisioning/template identity. Measurement binding also uses
  builder/profile/snapshot identity. Service composition never selects a cluster
  by overwriting ambient credentials. PostgreSQL, objects and renderer ownership
  remain independent; borrowed services survive logical release.
- The existing scheduler/admission owner charges physical startup separately from
  residency. Cluster claims persist through idle lifetime and physical settlement.
  A waiting pooled borrower yields provisional renderer/stack reservations when
  host admission is withdrawn, then reacquires exact current resident identities.
  Active borrowers remain pinned. Idle retirement can therefore recover capacity
  without a new scheduler, global lock, higher ceiling or changed deadline.
- Any unhealthy borrower immediately quarantines its allocation affinity, including
  while siblings remain active. No replacement may reach the same service binding
  before settlement. Partial provider ownership returns to the broker on startup
  failure, so primary failure, cleanup and quarantine remain coherent. Physical
  cluster close and residency release run once in order; failed physical cleanup
  retains residency and recovery proof. Unrelated affinities may still proceed.
- Recovery keeps immutable port intents and separately published declined/released
  outcomes. A declined foreign collision cannot acquire authority on a later retry;
  unsettled missing proof fails closed. Whole-run recovery may delegate dead-service
  browser namespace destruction to exactly proved owned parents after process and
  listener settlement; borrowed/measurement namespaces retain their live cleanup
  rules. Database/bucket dependents settle before their physical parents, and
  residency releases only after physical cleanup. This does not turn old CI failures
  into successes or authorize broad container deletion.
- Scratch defaults to machine-cache/harness-scratch independently of TMPDIR, with
  explicit external absolute override. Successful owners clean immediately. Bounded
  stale cleanup requires age, safe private ownership and a proven-dead process;
  live, unknown, sealed/finalizing or unresolved recovery state is retained. The
  original tmpfs capacity issue is not evidence of faulty underlying storage.
- Diagnostics retain per-service clocks, generation and completeness before cluster
  shutdown. Canonical lifecycle facts distinguish not-launched work from missing
  artifacts required after launch. Raw credentials, endpoint tokens and unbounded
  errors are excluded. Primary admission/startup/cleanup failures remain separate
  from secondary diagnostics and derived summaries. Old schema artifacts remain
  investigation evidence with no reader/writer aliases or qualification translation.
- Semantic row IDs and public Make commands are preserved where claims are unchanged;
  the recorded mixed-row/schema crosswalks identify actual cutovers. Human review of
  specification projection remains distinct from tests. The controlled reset file
  counts establish removal of relation-replacement work; timing remains descriptive,
  and exclusive PostgreSQL clusters do not isolate shared host CPU or storage.

Read-only source review identifies a further admission hypothesis: pooled work
calls TryAcquireWithResidents, which withdraws its queued host request on every
miss; the next loop creates a new token/sequence after releasing logical slots.

withdrawal may repeatedly lose the browser request's queue position. This is not
proven to explain this CI failure. Require terminal lifecycle/resource evidence
and a bounded deterministic priority/refresh reproduction before any correction.

capacity while queued, fresh resident identities after retirement, cancellation
settlement, active borrower protection, and cleanup/quiet progress. No new scheduler,

Source confirms an avoidable-work mechanism: a pooled host-admission miss releases
its logical renderer reservation; an incompatible waiter can retire an unallocated
slot and create another identity. Alternating incompatible waiters can repeat this
without provisioning a renderer. Residency intent and retirement publication
perform real private/public metadata work. Existing residency ensure caching
prevents repeated publication for the same identity, but retirement creates a new
identity and defeats that cache. No claim yet links this churn causally to the
PostgreSQL sync delay. The durable correction candidate is a bounded provisional
renderer lifetime plus preserved existing admission priority, with deterministic
proof before changing code. Preserve real physical compatibility, immutable proof,
active borrowers, capacity accounting, cancellation and cleanup; do not paper over
this with longer waits, extra locks or a second scheduler. Defer any additional
database-cleanup semantic change until this confirmed acquisition churn is repaired
and its impact is characterized.

Rationale: admission order belongs to the existing host kernel, while temporary
logical ownership belongs to the existing fixture owner. Releasing a renderer slot
must not silently create a new queue position. An unstarted logical slot has no
physical profile/trust state to destroy; actual physical generations still require
exact compatibility and settlement. Keep those lifetimes explicit instead of
adding global locks, retries, another queue, or larger budgets.

contention/ownership tests, generated projections only if their authored contracts
change, and this handoff. Compatibility: internal API/semantics cutover; public Make
commands and semantic rows remain stable. Remove the replaced try-and-withdraw
path rather than maintaining two policies. A pending request holds no active or
prospective capacity; resident claims remain with actual owned physical resources.
Do not permit resident identity changes after grant or weaken immutable recovery
proofs. A queue-generation/schema cutover, if required by the final design, must
reject incompatible live state explicitly rather than silently translate it.

Validation must prove that later fitting arrivals cannot starve an older feasible
request, that provisional releases permit pressure retirement, and that a later
queued dedicated renderer cannot hold the only slot needed by an older waiter.
It must also preserve impossible-claim rejection, bounded drain entitlement,
measurement fences, owner-loss recovery, cancellation settlement and physical
claims after uncertain cleanup. Compare structural publication/launch counts
separately from elapsed time. The contribution of confirmed renderer churn to the
exclusive PostgreSQL DataFileSync timeout remains unproved; that failure has its
own acceptance obligation and cannot be closed by these regressions alone.
